solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird: irrational figure in coal mine

indicators.note: 'in' places the figure inside the mine, as a miner is in the pit

parts.note: a coal mine is a pit; it opens after its first two letters
pi is the classic irrational number

explanation.surface: A strange account of a bird turning up down a coal mine, like the proverbial canary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' sounds like an insult but is exact mathematics: a number that cannot be written as a fraction. The answer's stutter is the clue that one piece sits inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain category definition: the pipit is a small brown songbird of fields and moors.

clue.text: A pregnant soprano losing lead in Puccini having developed unacceptable figure

indicators.note: something that has developed has changed its form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
losing says a letter is dropped from the words before them
the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An expectant soprano in a Puccini opera has changed shape and become a figure nobody wants on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P (the lead in Puccini) out of A PREGNANT SOPRANO and rearrange the fifteen letters that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona non grata is a person who is not welcome or acceptable, an unwelcome individual.

clue.text: Trial scheme bringing in electric current

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the scheme takes the current inside it

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for current

explanation.surface: A trial scheme to connect some district to the electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: I for current is standard physics notation and a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilot is used as an adjective here, as in a pilot scheme: a small trial run before the real thing.

clue.text: Tense? My rising alarm shuts out constant sources of drumming

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word above is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

indicators.note: shuts out means a letter is excluded from the word for alarm

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, as the speed of light in physics

explanation.surface: A tense moment as a rising alarm cuts out the steady beat of the drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MY into YM; 'shuts out' removes C (constant) from PANIC to leave PANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tympani are kettledrums, the instruments that produce drumming in an orchestra.

clue.text: Stretch limo shortened it to make deadline

parts.note: a stretch is time served in prison

indicators.note: 'shortened' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: A chauffeur trims a stretch limo so it can beat a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch limo' is a single phrase in the surface; split it, and stretch is a prison sentence, which is time.
explanation.definitionFit: A close synonym: a deadline is the point by which work must be done, the time allowed running out.

clue.text: Considerable trouble in darkest Yorkshire at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone warns of considerable trouble in the gloomy depths of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Considerable' feels far from neatness, but tidy has a second, informal sense of large.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British sense: a tidy sum is a considerable one.

clue.text: Obstinate type trimmed US magazine to help rising use of many information outlets

indicators.note: trimmed means cut back, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a mule is a stubborn person
Time is an American news magazine

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A stubborn person shortens an American magazine to help it rise in the media.
explanation.walkthrough: MULE is trimmed to MUL; AID rising gives DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Multimedia describes communication using several channels at once, such as text, sound and video.

clue.text: Scoundrel losing head in American city opera house

indicators.note: 'in' places the shortened word inside the city's letters
'losing head' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: A villain loses his head at an American opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the opera house in America; La Scala is in Milan, and LA merely wraps around the rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: La Scala in Milan is one of the world's most famous opera houses.

clue.text: Man penning newspaper's last stories about French city

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as sheep in a pen, so man encloses the rest
a word's last is its final letter

parts.note: a man is a male; it opens after MA

indicators.note: 'about' as in turned about, so the stories face the other way

explanation.surface: A journalist writing up the final stories of a newspaper about a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stories' are lies, as in telling stories to cover up. 'Penning' pretends to mean writing, which suits the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Marseille is France's great Mediterranean port.

clue.text: Astonished and attracted to almost certain start of presidential revolt

parts.note: to be taken by something is to be attracted to it

indicators.note: almost means the word for certain loses its final letter
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a revolt is a rising, a rise against rulers

explanation.surface: Someone astonished and drawn to the near-certain beginnings of a revolt against a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SURE to SUR; P is the start of presidential.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken by surprise is to be caught off guard, so astonished and startled.

clue.text: Electronic form in register is a good example

indicators.note: 'in' places the form inside the register, as an entry sits in a book

parts.note: a roll is a register of names; it opens after ROL
a mode is a form or manner

explanation.surface: An electronic form filed in the register counts as a good example.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like office paperwork; 'Electronic form' must split into E and MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a role model is a person others copy because they set a good example.

clue.text: Film franchise? I will avoid Scream

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so I keeps out of the scream

explanation.surface: A film franchise named, and someone vowing not to watch Scream, the horror series.
explanation.walkthrough: Scream is itself a horror film franchise, so the capital S pulls the eye away from the plain verb shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shrek is the animated ogre film series with several sequels.

clue.text: Expense from parts of arrangement being switched?

indicators.note: things that are switched swap places, so the two halves change round

parts.note: a layout is an arrangement, made of the parts LAY and OUT

explanation.surface: A cost arising because parts of some arrangement were swapped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' tells you the arrangement word is built from two smaller words, and 'switched' swaps them; the question mark flags that the definition comes by an unusual route.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outlay is money laid out, an expense.

clue.text: Branch bearing a half-Andean vegetable

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: a limb is a branch of a tree

indicators.note: half the word is kept, here its last three of six letters

explanation.surface: A branch carrying a part-Andean vegetable, a nod to the plant's South American origins.
explanation.walkthrough: LIMB bearing A gives LIMAB; add EAN, the back half of ANDEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The lima bean is a broad flat edible bean, named after the capital of Peru.

clue.text: Branch of medicine that could make you stay chirpy

indicators.note: the letters could make, that is be rearranged into, the answer

explanation.surface: A branch of medicine that promises to keep you cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a description of the answer, since psychiatry aims to keep patients well in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: psychiatry is the medical specialty treating mental illness.

clue.text: Agree cops should release head of Roman church

indicators.note: releasing a letter lets it go from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: to cop something is to get or obtain it, so cops means acquires

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Police being asked to free the leader of a Roman church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cops' is a verb here, not police: it means gets, ACQUIRES, from which the R (head of Roman) is released to leave ACQUIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquiesce is to accept or consent quietly, which is to agree without protest.

clue.text: Question over description of sea omitting one island in equation

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
omitting means leaving out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Adriatic is the adjective describing the sea between Italy and the Balkans
I is an abbreviation for island, and only one of the two is dropped

explanation.surface: A question about naming a sea, with one island missing from the equation.
explanation.walkthrough: ADRIATIC has two I's; omitting one gives ADRATIC, placed under QU.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadratic is an equation in which the highest power of the unknown is a square.

clue.text: Mixture of everything two-thirds of crossword solvers recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards
two of the three letters are kept, the first two

parts.note: crossword solvers are addressed as you

explanation.surface: A survey finds that most crossword solvers remembered something about a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often stand for their solvers with 'you', as if speaking to the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy is a metal made by combining two or more elements, so a blend.

clue.text: Acceptable area to house South African in Japanese city

indicators.note: to house someone is to give them a home inside, so the outer letters hold the South African

parts.note: OK = acceptable; it opens after O

explanation.surface: A suitable district to house a South African living in a Japanese city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acceptable area' reads as one estate agent's phrase; it is two pieces that between them make the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Osaka is Japan's big commercial city on Honshu.

clue.text: Supply heater's source of wood

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, in a bending way, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters with the S

explanation.surface: An instruction to supply a heater with its fuel of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as the verb provide; here it is the adverb from supple, so the letters bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the ash tree is a common source of timber and firewood.

clue.text: Cut deal with university after money and drink

indicators.note: after puts the following pieces behind the word for money
cut means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to treat is to deal with something

explanation.surface: A student gets a cut-price deal, then spends the cash on a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is a verb here, as in dealing with or handling a matter, and 'with' simply joins the next piece on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Flaxen fibres gently touch hard walking surface

parts.note: tow is the coarse fibre of flax or hemp
to pat is to touch gently

explanation.surface: Flax fibres lightly brushing a hard path underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Tow is a less familiar word: the short coarse fibres left from processing flax.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a towpath runs beside a canal, where horses once towed barges, and is now walked.

clue.text: Composer, German, with quiet success

explanation.surface: A composer, German by birth, enjoying quiet success.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a German composer, but Gershwin was American.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: George Gershwin wrote Rhapsody in Blue.

clue.text: Just appear pale, in the grip of drink

indicators.note: something held in a grip is enclosed, so drink holds pale inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink; it opens after S

explanation.surface: Someone who looks pale and seems to be in the grip of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' carries the sense of the phrase: to swan up is to turn up casually, as if without a care.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal idiom: to swan up is to arrive nonchalantly, simply to appear.

clue.text: Radiant, unconfined free spirit

indicators.note: the outer letters are the confining walls, so removing them leaves the word unconfined
letters set free are no longer held in their order

parts.note: RADIANT without its outer letters R and T

explanation.surface: A radiant free spirit, not confined by anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free spirit' reads as one phrase, but 'free' is the anagram signal and 'spirit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, a spirit of rivers and springs.

clue.text: I fish, letting nothing escape is key

indicators.note: letting something escape means removing it from the word
escape completes the instruction that nothing gets out of the fish

parts.note: O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: An angler explains that letting no catch get away is the key to fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLE lets its O (nothing) escape to leave SLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a low island, especially in the Caribbean.

clue.text: A lot of maps moving westward end of water table

indicators.note: in an across clue moving westward means read from right to left, backwards
a lot of a word, though not all, means it loses its last letter

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Maps shifting west to show where the water table ends.
explanation.walkthrough: ATLAS loses its last letter to give ATLA, which turned westward becomes ALTA; R ends water.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the communion table in a church, or the raised surface for offerings.

clue.text: Italian maestro's Italian opera: popular, repeatedly returning

indicators.note: done repeatedly means done more than once, so the word is used twice
coming back means going the other way, so each copy is reversed

explanation.surface: An Italian conductor's favourite opera, a hit that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay. The two 'Italian's are separate words: one in the definition, one describing the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Arturo Toscanini was the great Italian conductor, and maestro is the title for one.

clue.text: Cheap tyre burst, for example

indicators.note: a burst tyre flies apart, and so do its letters

explanation.surface: A cheap tyre that blew out, held up as a warning example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' reads as a stock phrase; split it, and 'for' links while 'example' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A close synonym: an archetype is the original or model example of which others are copies.

clue.text: Start of hundred inch garden feature?

indicators.note: a word's start is its first letter

parts.note: to inch is to edge forward slowly

explanation.surface: A garden feature starting at a hundred inches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inch' looks like a measurement to go with 'hundred', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a hedge is a row of bushes forming a garden boundary.
